case_title: Main Pal v. State of Haryana
accused_victim_relationship: Neighbour (house about 15-16 houses away per witnesses); alleged prior dispute over a water course with the complainant's son, per defence witness DW-1. Court made no finding on the dispute.
evidence_type: Eyewitness testimony of the complainant and her daughter-in-law; FIR statement; investigating officer's evidence (PW-3)
trial_court_outcome: Convicted under ss.452 and 354 IPC; six months rigorous imprisonment and fine of Rs.1,000 (default one month simple imprisonment)
high_court_outcome: Criminal revision dismissed; conviction upheld; sentence reduced to four months rigorous imprisonment
neutral_facts: On a night in March 1996, the complainant and her daughter-in-law were sleeping in the complainant's house at about 11.30 PM. No adult male was in the house apart from children. The accused jumped over the front wall, broke the outside bulbs and ran away. Around 12.30 AM the accused returned by scaling the door and caught the daughter-in-law's hand. She raised an alarm and the complainant woke up, after which the accused ran away. The complainant's FIR statement and testimony described the incident this way. The daughter-in-law identified the accused and gave evidence of both visits. In cross-examination, the complainant and the daughter-in-law agreed the accused had not touched, teased or abused the complainant and had not gone towards or spoken to her. Both said the accused lived 15-16 houses away and the families were not on visiting terms. A defence witness, the former village sarpanch, said a quarrel over a water course with the complainant's son had turned into the complaint. The police investigated the complaint and submitted a report under Section 173 of the Code.
physical_harm: No injury mentioned; alleged catching of daughter-in-law's hand and breaking of outside bulbs
financial_property_loss: Not applicable (only breaking of outside bulbs alleged; no value stated)
premeditation_planning: Not stated (charge alleged preparation for hurt or assault; court made no finding)
motive: alleged: a water-course quarrel with the complainant's son, per defence witness DW-1; the court did not decide motive
key_evidence_accepted: Testimony of PW-1 and PW-2 as elicited in cross-examination, that the accused caught the daughter-in-law's hand and ran away when she raised an alarm; the court relied on the record of what the evidence showed rather than making a fresh finding of guilt
witness_credibility: Not assessed by the court on credibility; the court noted the complainant's admission that the accused did not touch, tease or abuse her
post_offence_conduct: Ran away after the alarm was raised, as described in the evidence; no other post-offence conduct stated
trial_duration: offence: 22/23.3.1996 (night of incident; FIR registered 23.3.1996); trial judgment: 2.2.2001; High Court: 16.3.2010; Supreme Court: 07.09.2010
legal_representation: Appellant: Vikas Sharma, K.M. Gupta, Praveen Swarup. State counsel: Not stated
investigation_status: FIR registered 23.3.1996; police investigation completed and report submitted under s.173 CrPC; trial held
procedural_irregularity: Charge named the mother-in-law (PW-1) as the victim, while the evidence concerned the daughter-in-law; the court held this a material error causing prejudice
appeal_history: Trial court (Magistrate, 2.2.2001): convicted under ss.452 and 354 IPC, six months RI. Sessions appeal (Addl. Sessions Judge, 20.2.2002): dismissed. High Court (revision, 16.3.2010): conviction upheld, sentence reduced to four months RI. Supreme Court: appeal allowed, conviction set aside, new trial directed
prosecution_argument: Not stated in the Supreme Court judgment; the lower courts held that an accused cannot take advantage of a technical defect in the charge
defence_argument: The charge named the complainant but the evidence concerned the daughter-in-law; the accused was not required to defend that charge, so he should be acquitted
legal_principle_applied: Ss.211, 212, 215 and 464 CrPC: an accused must know the exact charge; an error in the charge is fatal only where it misled the accused and caused failure of justice; courts apply a broad vision looking to substance and fair trial
precedent_relied_upon: Willie (William) Slaney v. State of Madhya Pradesh AIR 1956 SC 116; Gurbachan Singh v. State of Punjab AIR 1957 SC 623; Shamsaheb M. Multtani v. State of Karnataka (2001) 2 SCC 577; State of West Bengal v. Laisal Haque AIR 1989 SC 129; State of A.P. v. Thakkidiram Reddy (1998) 6 SCC 554; Dalbir Singh v. State of UP (2004) 5 SCC 334; Dumpala Chandra Reddy v. Nimakayala Bali Reddy (2008) 8 SCC 339; Sanichar Sahni v. State of Bihar (2009) 7 SCC 198. State of Himachal Pradesh v. Geeta Ram (2000) 7 SCC 452 distinguished
other_sentence_order: New trial directed after framing a charge substituting 'her daughter-in-law Sheela Devi' for 'abovenamed Prakashi Devi' in the second part of the charge
